title: End of Act I
description: The survey is dealt with, one way or another, and the valley has gone quiet in the way a room does after somebody has said the thing out loud.

the_flagon.title: A word at the Flagon
the_flagon.objective: This part is over. Return to the Golden Flagon and sit down with Mara Hearthstone.
the_flagon.journal: The survey is dealt with, and Rivermark is still standing. That doesn't mean it's safe. Mara wants a word, and I have a fair idea what about.

end_took.title: End of Act I: Kept
end_took.journal: I kept the survey. Nine sheets, with Rivermark listed on the sixth as a cost. Nobody in the valley has the standing to demand it back. Mara says paper like that goes downriver on Tull's boat on the second and fifth. I think she's right about where it goes.

end_burned.title: End of Act I: Burned
end_burned.journal: I burned the survey. Three years of chain-work went up in the rain. The Concern will start again and ask who stood by the fire. Mara says that kind of asking comes upriver on Tull's boat on the second and fifth. I'd rather be aboard going the other way.

end_sold.title: End of Act I: Sold back
end_sold.journal: I sold the survey back for five hundred gold, plus a retainer of forty a quarter for services not described. Mara looked at the purse, then looked away. A retainer doesn't pay for sitting still. Tull's boat goes downriver on the second and fifth, and I expect to be aboard.

end_warned.title: End of Act I: Read out
end_warned.journal: Pyke read the survey aloud on Granary Row, and Reed wrote it all down. Rivermark now knows its assessed value and that there's nothing it can do. Mara says the answer to what comes next is on Tull's boat on the second and fifth. Someone downriver wrote that figure. Someone downriver can answer for it.
